review_briefs.r3look:
The merged build in first person. Game-boy plays in first person; side view only checks mechanics. The gap reviewer judged the build at 8f5519f in first person (/Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-gap/captures/review_gap/, with its probe gap_probe.gd/.tscn: the W*, KO*, K*, U1, P1 and G* acts). The round 2 fixers recorded their own after-captures (paths in fix-r2-*.json); judge the merged build independently, and compare where useful.
Record (one Godot process at a time; copy gap_probe.gd/.tscn into your captures folder and fix its paths; the KO view fixer's probe is /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-fix-r2-player-ko-view/captures/fix/ko_probe.tscn and its script):
1. Launches into walls, building fronts and the curb (probe W1-W10) and the uppercut from behind (U1), in first person (side view for mechanics only): the head stays out of the wall, the body hits and crumples, the from-behind launch pitches forward away from the lens, nothing within 0.25 m of the lens or over half the view; the point-blank throw into a wall (W4/W5) as before. Note what the fixer left: the hook's fists in a corner (0.14 m, about 61% of the view, from the step-in against a pinned dummy) and the curb's straight rise and drop.
2. The player's KO, the out-of-body view (KO1-KO6: standing, KO'd while holding with a second dummy jabbing, facing a wall, hit from behind): the ease out from the eyes, the framing (the whole body lying on the floor, unclipped, with room), the hold, the ease back in on the get-up with no pop; the released victim stays out of the lens; the first-person parts hide again exactly when the lens is back; nothing passes close to the lens (the lead saw the player's own head large for a frame or two of the return). Judge it as a player: does it read as a short out-of-body moment; is it too fast, too slow, too far, too close? Also record one player knockdown that isn't a KO (the fixer's KD1), for Game-boy's open question.
3. The comeback: a dummy KO'd beside an occupied post (K3, in first person and side) comes back clear of the player, in front of or beside him, and waits instead of walking into him; simultaneous KOs (K1/K2) still come back together.
4. The hook stagger in first person (side for mechanics): the re-posed far arm stays bent near the guard; the fling and the trunk's rock-back still read; whether the far hand's sag after the fling looks wrong.
5. Every first-person finisher after hit-04 and the warm-up (combo_bot 'P · P', 'P P · P', 'K · K', 'P P K', 'Hold P, release: haymaker', 'Pipe: pick up, 3 swings, throw'): the 2 flash frames after the impact frame, and nothing visible at load (look at the first second of a fresh run frame by frame for any ink frame, burst or sprite; the warm-up draws one ink pixel for one frame).
6. The damage looks after perf-02 (vfx_bot's damage-look acts): CLEAN, BRUISED and BLOODIED as before (compare with the hit reviewer's sheets under /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-hit/captures/).
7. Every first-person ragdoll_bot act on the merged build (--act=a|b now works in every bot), against the gap reviewer's rag_all sheets: anything that changed and shouldn't have.
Return the 3-6 most telling first-person sheets for Game-boy in sheets_for_game_boy (the KO view among them), and put measured numbers (nearest distance to the lens, share of the view) in the evidence.

common_note: ROUND 2's FIXES are merged into m2/hit-feel at 72a1066 (518/518 tests, no SCRIPT ERROR or ERROR; tuning/default.json regenerated, 318 values). r2-launch-into-walls (gap-01, gap-03, gap-07, gap-08 d): a launch whose capsule is blocked by a wall, a crate or the curb hands over to the full ragdoll at once from the pose on screen, and the hips pull loosens while the capsule is stopped in flight (ragdoll_wall_reach_m, ragdoll_hips_blocked_hz); a launch from behind takes over at once too, so it pitches away from the attacker; Ragdoll.start() seeds its drawn-pose cache on a new ragdoll's first tick (after the kick's part-body search, on purpose); grab_release_blend_s and reaction_snap_blend_s replace script constants. r2-vfx-first-use (perf-01, perf-02, gap-08 e): a windowed-only load-time warm-up of the comic sprite variants and the impact frame (it draws one pixel of the ink frame for one frame); the damage look's detail layer is always on, CLEAN being a transparent texture, so a look change never switches the shader variant. r2-player-ko-view (gap-02): the player's out-of-body KO view in game/camera/first_person_camera.gd, tunables in Camera > 'KO view'. r2-dummy-comeback (gap-05, gap-04, gap-08 a-c): respawn rings spaced by dummy_respawn_gap_m, ties broken toward the player's view, return_home waits for room and stops when stuck; ko_blink_duty and return_home's numbers are tunables; the sideways stagger's far arm is re-posed bent near the guard. Each fixer's outcomes, remaining items and spec questions are in fix-r2-*.json. The lead fixed gap-09 (bots) and, after the merge, relaxed test_ragdoll.gd's hook arm-trail ratio from 0.8 to 0.85: with the re-posed far arm the drawn far hand sags about 0.22 m under its raised pose at 0.45 arm influence (each branch alone passed); the lead judged the merged hook in first person as fine (captures/lead_r2merge/hook_fp.png in the main checkout). WAITING ON GAME-BOY (new spec questions; report, don't implement): the player's non-KO knockdowns get no KO view (the belly slab covers the view for about 1.3 s); the HUD centre dot and HP bar during the KO view; a wall reaction beyond the crumple (deflect, splat, bounce; default: the body stops at the wall and drops); the push's part-body choice by contact (it reads a stale cache today; choosing by contact would cut the hook's give from 0.32 to 0.22 m).
